messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into French, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE French line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Il la chassera à travers chaque ville, jusqu’à ce qu’il l’ait remise en enfer, là où l’envie l’a d’abord envoyée.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------|------------------------|--------| | Questi | demonstrative pronoun, subject (the male agent) | **Il** | “he” | OK | | la | clitic pronoun, accusative, feminine singular (patient) | **la** | “her” | OK | | caccerà | verb *cacciare* future 3 sg (“will hunt”) | **chassera** | “will hunt” | OK | | per | preposition “through, across” | **à travers** | “through” | OK | | ogne | determiner “every” (archaic *ogni*) | **chaque** | “every” | OK | | villa | noun, feminine singular “town, village” | **ville** | “town” | OK | | fin | subordinating conjunction “until” | **jusqu’à** | “until” | OK | | che | complementizer introducing clause “that” | **ce** (as part of *ce qu’il*) | “that” | OK | | l'avrà | clitic + auxiliary future perfect “will have (him) …” | **l’ait** (subjunctive perfect) | “that he will have” | OK | | rimessa | past participle of *rimettere* “set back” | **remise** | “set back” | OK | | ne | preposition “in, into” (archaic form) | **en** | “in” | OK | | lo | masculine singular definite article before *‘nferno* | *(none)* – article omitted in French | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | 'nferno | noun “hell” (inferno) | **enfer** | “hell” | OK | | là | adverb of place “there” | **là** | “there” | OK | | onde | relative adverb “whence, where” | **où** | “where” | OK | | 'nvidia | noun “envy” (personified) | **l’envie** | “envy” | OK | | prima | adverb of time “first, initially” | **d’abord** | “first” | OK | | dipartilla | verb *dipartire* future 3 sg with clitic “‑la” “shall send her forth” | **l’a envoyée** | “shall send her forth” | OK |
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **lo** – marked **UNNECESSARY**: the masculine article before *‘nferno* is naturally omitted in French (*enfer* does not take an article in this construction). No other missing, wrong, or grammatical‑error items were found.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only French script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final French text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
